stories.title: Shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square Leaves Six Dead and Over a Dozen Injured
stories.summary: A shooting incident in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland, resulted in six fatalities and at least 15 injuries. The gunman, a Polish citizen, reportedly opened fire from his car before being shot and wounded by police. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding this tragic event, which is notable as mass shootings are rare in Poland.
stories.event_title: Shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square Leaves Six Dead and Over a Dozen Injured

story_report.summary: Six people were killed and at least 15 wounded after a Polish citizen allegedly opened fire from a car in Kraków’s Main Market Square area on Nov. 7. The attack occurred around 3 p.m. near Sławkowska Street, prompting the city to activate its crisis staff as emergency services responded. Police shot and detained the suspect near the Dietla–Stradomska intersection; he was later reported hospitalized. The scale of the attack was unusual in Poland, where mass shootings are uncommon.

stories.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña Impeached and Arrested Amid Banking Crisis
stories.summary: Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest following a banking crisis that left nearly three million customers unable to access their funds. The Senate voted unanimously for his removal over allegations related to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as the new president, pledging to compensate those affected by the crisis.
stories.event_title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña Impeached and Arrested Amid Banking Crisis

story_report.summary: Paraguay’s Senate removed Santiago Peña from office and he was placed under house arrest as a banking crisis affecting nearly three million customers deepened. Pedro Alliana was sworn in to replace him, taking charge of the immediate political response while Congress moved to speed limited deposit-insurance payments for Ueno customers. The change of government does not settle questions over losses beyond insured deposits or potential criminal proceedings linked to the crisis.

The court found that he incited his followers to starve themselves and their families in a bid to 'meet Jesus.' Mackenzie and 28 accomplices were convicted for their roles in this tragic incident.

The sentence followed a finding that religious teaching and a church hierarchy were used to compel fasting until death, while Mackenzie and several co-defendants have begun an appeal.

stories.title: ANC Faces Significant Decline in South African Local Elections
stories.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive less than a third of the vote in South Africa's local elections, marking a significant decline from previous years. With over 80% of ballots counted, the ANC is on track for its worst-ever election performance, estimated at around 32%. This decline is attributed to widespread voter dissatisfaction over issues such as water outages and power cuts, leading to potential coalition challenges in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.
stories.event_title: South Africans Vote in Tense Local Elections Amid Discontent

story_report.summary: South Africa’s African National Congress was projected to win under 32% of the vote in local elections, with more than 80% of ballots counted placing it at 31.8%, nearly 14 percentage points below its 2021 result. The provisional outcome would be the party’s worst electoral performance to date and left several major councils, including Johannesburg and Tshwane, hung or unresolved. The immediate consequence is likely coalition bargaining over control of key municipalities, rather than a single national governing outcome.

Nearly 50 people were reported missing and may be trapped beneath the rubble as rescue operations continued. President Volodymyr Zelensky described the attack as a “vile terrorist attack,” while the UN said it was still verifying the precise civilian casualty toll.
